subtopics.title: The Plane, the Points, and the Distance Formula

questions.question: The distance formula is a coordinate version of:
options: The gradient formula
The theorem of Pythagoras
The averaging rule
Congruent triangles

questions.question: For A(−1; 3) and B(5; 11), the horizontal difference is:
options: 6 units, because 5 − (−1) = 5 + 1
4 units
−4 units
16 units

questions.question: The length of AB for A(−1; 3) and B(5; 11) is:
options: √14 units
100 units
14 units
10 units

questions.question: Why is the distance from B to A the same as the distance from A to B?
options: Because coordinates are always positive
Because the formula adds the coordinates
Because each difference is squared, and squaring erases the sign
Because distances are rounded off

questions.question: The midpoint of the segment joining A(−1; 3) and B(5; 11) is:
Which statement correctly separates the three formulae?
options: Midpoint is the only one that ADDS the coordinates; distance and gradient subtract
Distance is the only one that adds
Gradient adds; the other two subtract
All three formulae subtract

questions.question: M(2; 7) is the midpoint of AB and A is (−1; 3). The coordinates of B are:
The diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other exactly when:
options: The diagonals are equal in length
Both diagonals have the SAME midpoint
The diagonals have gradients multiplying to −1
All four sides are equal

questions.question: The gradient of the line through A(−1; 3) and B(5; 11) is:
The gradient of a VERTICAL line is:
options: Undefined, because the change in x is zero and division by zero has no meaning
Zero
One
Infinity, written as a number

questions.question: A line has gradient 4/3. A line perpendicular to it has gradient:
options: −3/4, the negative reciprocal

questions.question: P(2; 1), Q(4; 7) and R(6; 13) are collinear because:
options: Gradient PQ = gradient QR = 3, and the segments share the point Q
PQ and QR are equal in length only
Q is the origin
All three points have positive coordinates

questions.question: For A(−1; 3), B(5; 11), C(10; 8) and D(4; 0), the lengths AB and CD are both:
options: √34 units
10 units
14 units
8 units

questions.question: The diagonals AC and BD of that quadrilateral both have midpoint:
Gradient AB × gradient AD = 4/3 × (−3/5) = −4/5. This shows that ABCD is:
options: NOT a rectangle, because the product is not −1, so angle A is not a right angle
A rectangle
A square
A kite

questions.question: Which conclusion about ABCD is fully justified by the calculations?
options: It is a square, because its diagonals bisect
It is a rectangle, because the sketch looks square-cornered
It is a rhombus, because AB = CD
It is a parallelogram and nothing more — opposite sides equal and parallel, diagonals bisecting, but no right angle and no four equal sides

subtopics.title: Eight Blocks Across, Six Blocks Up

questions.question: The library is eight blocks east and six blocks north. Walking the streets is 14 blocks. Cutting straight across the fields is:
options: 14 blocks
10 blocks
12 blocks
48 blocks

questions.question: The unchanging recipe for a distance on the grid is:
options: Find the across, find the up, square both, add, and take the square root
Add the across and the up, then halve
Divide the up by the across
Multiply the across by the up and halve

questions.question: A distance can never come out negative because:
options: Coordinates are never negative
You always start from the origin
Squaring wipes out every minus sign before the square root is taken
Blocks are counted in whole numbers

questions.question: Two friends live at house numbers 5 and 17. They meet halfway, at house number:
The memory rule that separates the three formulae is:
options: Middle means ADD and halve; distance and steepness mean SUBTRACT
Middle means subtract; distance means add
All three formulae add
Steepness means add and halve

questions.question: Your midpoint answer lands OUTSIDE the two given points. The most likely cause is:
options: The two points are too close together
You subtracted where you should have added
You forgot to square the differences
The points were labelled in the wrong order

questions.question: Two roads cross, and each is cut exactly in half at the crossing. On the grid this shows up as:
options: The two roads having equal lengths
One road being horizontal
Both roads having the SAME midpoint
Gradients that multiply to −1

subtopics.title: Steepness You Can Feel — and the Traps

questions.question: A gradient of 4/3 means:
options: For every 3 units across, the line climbs 4 units up
The line drops 4 for every 3 across
The line is 4/3 of a unit long
The line makes an angle of 43 degrees

questions.question: A netball court is flat and the school hall's wall is straight up. Their gradients are:
options: Both zero
Zero for the court, undefined for the wall
Undefined for the court, zero for the wall
Both undefined

questions.question: On the grid, the only accepted proof of a right angle is:
options: The corner looking square in your sketch
The two sides having equal lengths
The two gradients being equal
The two gradients multiplying to give −1

questions.question: A learner puts the second point's y on top but the first point's x underneath when computing a gradient. The result is:
options: Correct, since order never matters for gradient
Undefined
Wrong — mixing the order flips the sign, turning a rising line into a falling one
Correct, but only when both coordinates are positive
